## What you'll find here {#whats-here}

<dl class="kinds">
<div><dt><a href="workflows/index.html">Workflows</a></dt><dd>Step-by-step procedures for a research task, with the exact prompts and the checks to run on the result.</dd></div>
<div><dt><a href="prompts/index.html">Prompts</a></dt><dd>Single prompts that worked on real research tasks, with an example of the output and their known limits.</dd></div>
<div><dt><a href="skills/index.html">Skills</a></dt><dd>Packaged instructions and scripts that an AI agent loads when a task needs them, ready to install.</dd></div>
<div><dt><a href="agent-configs/index.html">Agent configs</a></dt><dd>CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md templates that teach coding agents the conventions of a research project.</dd></div>
<div><dt><a href="model-checks/index.html">Model checks</a></dt><dd>Small, repeatable tests of models on real scientific tasks, with dated results.</dd></div>
<div><dt><a href="reviews/index.html">Reviews</a></dt><dd>Papers, guides and announcements about AI in science, read critically: what they claim and what holds up.</dd></div>
</dl>

Everything carries the same header: model, tool, date of the last test and verification level. Errors worth knowing about are collected in [Failures](failures/index.html).

## How this site works

::: {.principles}
:::: {}
### Test before trusting
Every workflow is run on a real research task before it is published, and says how to check what the model produced.
::::
:::: {}
### Date everything
Models change every few months. Each page records the model, the tool and the date of the last test.
::::
:::: {}
### Publish the failures
Where a model got it wrong, the page says so. The [Failures](failures/index.qmd) section collects the errors worth knowing about.
::::
:::: {}
### Keep it open
Text is CC BY 4.0, code is MIT, and anyone can propose a workflow through GitHub. See [Contribute](contribute.qmd).
::::
:::
